design_rationale: Rework round 2. One Advantage cardholder, two losses on the same account. In July her card was lost; a foreign online purchase was disputed by phone on the report day, the written confirmation never came, so no provisional credit was owed; it was resolved with an error found on 2026-10-20, more than 90 days after the notice, and its final credit is still owed (171.36). In late September her replacement card was stolen (learned 2026-09-26, reported late on 2026-10-01); the September 29 withdrawal claim was signed on 2026-10-09 and provisionally credited with 50.00 withheld, then resolved with an error found on 2026-10-14 with the late-report liability, so the part of its provisional credit above its due must be taken back (427.21). On 2026-10-14 she reported a second withdrawal of that loss by phone; today she signs its claim form (root, owner user, 191.95). Tree: claim form credit <- (state gate: the other claim of the same loss carries its reversal) reversal <- (value input: available balance; final credits owed on other lost or stolen card claims post first) final credit. Factors are the real dimensions of these credits on the Advantage plan schedules: Visa Zero Liability vs the timely/late Regulation E limits, liability already charged on the same loss, Paystride fees on the claimed transaction or the free withdrawal it used, the service, late-credit and investigation allowances, and the early pay the worker had to send to an outside destination on the report day while the card was blocked (Access ledger and tier).
user_scenario: You are Talia Rourke, a 38-year-old warehouse lead at Rio Verde Logistics in Glendale who is paid on a Paystride Visa Payroll Card. You are calling from your car before your shift, organized but tired of this. Your wallet with the card in it was stolen at the end of September; you reported the card on October 1 and got a new one. When you went over your card history afterwards you found a second ATM withdrawal of about two hundred dollars on September 30 that you had not made, and you called about it on October 14. You were told that before that money could go back on your card you would have to sign Paystride's claim form. That is what you want done today: sign the claim form and get the money for the September 30 withdrawal back on your card. You have no idea how the credit is worked out. Give your details only when the agent asks for them: your mobile number is 6025550173, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 5264, your date of birth is November 2, 1987, and your ZIP code is 85031. If the agent asks when you realized the card was gone, you say it was the morning of Saturday, September 26, but you thought you had left the wallet at your sister's and only called on October 1, and you admit that was a mistake. If the agent asks which withdrawal, it is the one on September 30 at the Canyon Market ATM, about two hundred dollars. If the agent asks for the card, the new one ends in 5918. If the agent says other items on your card account have to be settled before this credit can be done, you tell them that is fine and to take care of it; you do not argue about amounts you did not ask about, and if they tell you money is being taken back you ask them to make sure it is right and let it go. When the agent tells you how much will go back on the card for the September 30 withdrawal, you are unhappy it is not the full amount, but once they explain why, you accept it. When the agent hands you the claim form to sign, you sign it for exactly the claim and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation you get. Once the credit shows as posted, you thank the agent and end the call. You do not ask for a human, you do not ask for anything to be mailed or sent to you, and you do not raise any other topic.

request_binding.action_semantics: The July claim was resolved with an error found on 2026-10-20 and carries no credit, so its final credit is owed now; the take-back the customer's own credit waits on is not made until that final credit has posted.

discriminator.business_meaning: final credit on a resolved lost or stolen card claim carrying no credit

stage_provenance.fact: Investigation finished with an error found on 2026-10-20.

base_preconditions.condition: A final credit is posted only on a dispute whose status is resolved_error_found.
A dispute receives at most one final credit, and none when its provisional credit already stands.

gold_actions.business_effect: A provisional credit reversal posts against the September 29 claim, taking back what it was credited above what it is due.

request_binding.action_semantics: The September 29 claim of the same loss was resolved with an error found on 2026-10-14 and its provisional credit stands above what it is due; five business days have passed, so the reversal is owed, and the customer's claim form credit is fixed only after it carries that reversal.

discriminator.business_meaning: reversal of the excess of a provisional credit on a resolved claim

stage_provenance.fact: The final credit owed on the account's other lost or stolen card claim has posted, raising the balance the reversal can take.

base_preconditions.condition: A provisional credit is reversed only on a dispute whose status is resolved_no_error or resolved_error_found.

A provisional credit is reversed at most once.

base_preconditions.condition: A provisional credit is owed only when the notice arrives within error_notice_outer_limit_days calendar days after the disputed transaction's posted date, or, when later, within error_notice_window_days calendar days after the history access date.
A provisional credit is posted only while the dispute's status is investigating.
A dispute receives at most one provisional credit.
Cardholder liability for unauthorized transactions: Visa Zero Liability for purchases, the timely and late caps for a lost or stolen card, counted once per loss in posting order.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A provisional credit is owed only when the notice arrives within error_notice_outer_limit_days calendar days after the disputed transaction's posted date, or, when later, within error_notice_window_days calendar days after the history access date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Calendar days are counted from the day after the posted date or the history access date, and a notice arriving on the last day of either period is timely.

boundary_check.just_before: The withdrawal posted 2026-09-30; notice on 2026-10-14 is day 14 of the 120-day outer limit after posting (and day 13 after the 2026-10-01 history access).
boundary_check.at_boundary: A notice on 2027-01-28, the 120th day after posting, would still be timely (inclusive); one on 2027-01-29 would earn no provisional credit, the 60-day window after the history access having closed on 2026-11-30.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A provisional credit reversal posts only after provisional_reversal_notice_business_days business days have passed since the resolution date.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays, counted from the day after the resolution date.

boundary_check.just_before: The claim was resolved 2026-10-14; the five business days after it are 2026-10-15, 2026-10-16, 2026-10-19, 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21, so they have passed by today, 2026-10-22.
boundary_check.at_boundary: On 2026-10-21 the fifth business day was still running and no reversal could post; from 2026-10-22 it may.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's worker profile from the mobile number she gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the customer reference number of the cardholder.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Confirm identity with two matching credentials before discussing the card or moving money.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be confirmed before account information is discussed or any credit or reversal is booked.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the payroll card account: plan (Advantage), status, first deposit date, current available balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan selects the claim schedules and their limits and fees; the available balance is what a reversal may take.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every claim on the card: the October 14 phone claim on the September 30 withdrawal awaiting written confirmation, the September 29 claim of the same loss (resolved with an error found, provisional credit posted), the July lost-card claim (resolved with an error found, no credit), and the May claim resolved with no error.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The claim form credit waits on the other claim of the same loss carrying its reversal; that reversal waits on every final credit owed on the account's other lost or stolen card claims (the July claim has none).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the card ledger: the claimed withdrawals and purchase with their surcharges, surcharge rebate and Paystride fees, the own and claimed out-of-network withdrawals of the pay period that began 2026-09-25, the replacement card fees, the provisional credit on the September 29 claim and the May credit and reversal.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every factor of the three computations rests on these rows: fees, rebates and free withdrawals on each claimed transaction and the provisional credit standing on the September 29 claim.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's Payroll Card Program the account was opened under: package Advantage, live.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The card plan, and with it which claim schedules apply, follows the employer's package.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the replacement orders: lost card on 2026-07-21 (standard) and stolen card on 2026-10-01 (expedited).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The replacement ordered on a claim's notice date sets its report day and whether the card was replaced as lost or stolen.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the cardholder's Paystride Access plan: tier, status, next payday.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The early pay cost on a lost card is capped at the next-business-day bank fee of the tier the Access plan holds today.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Access ledger: the instant early pay transfers to an external debit card on 2026-07-21 and 2026-10-01 (report days, card blocked) and their fees, and the free transfer of 2026-09-28.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The early pay cost counted with the July final credit and in the September 29 claim's due is the fee booked on the report-day transfers.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's Access program agreement: live, fee model worker_paid.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Under the worker_paid fee model the instant-transfer fees were the worker's own cost.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (final credit -> reversal -> claim form credit) with no parallel edges: the reversal's sentence fixes the final credit first (it raises the balance the reversal can take: 483.83 after it, 312.47 before it), and the claim form credit's sentence fixes the reversal before it. No two writes are left unordered.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the final credit the balance stays 312.47, so the reversal computes 312.47 instead of 427.21 (limited by the balance), and the final credit row of 171.36 is missing from the terminal state.

Without the reversal the terminal state lacks the 427.21 reversal row against e86cd5e5-5278-405f-8f4b-3d6df23e1eb1 and the card balance ends 427.21 higher; the claim form credit itself still computes 191.95 because the liability already charged is read from the other claim's own fields (state gate).
